# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 21 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 21 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_021_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 13

**1** "Those from the sixth mountain, which had clefts and ravines, large and small — who are they?" "These are those who have the small clefts: they bear grudges against one another and are somewhat at variance with one another. Many of them grow weary because of their disputes. Nevertheless there is repentance for them, and those who repent will live to God. But those with the large clefts — these are those who quarrel constantly and nurse ill will toward one another. **2** These therefore are cast from the tower, and they are rejected. Repentance is difficult for such people, but if they repent they will have their place in the building, but if they do not repent they will perish." **3** "Those from the seventh mountain — the cheerful and flourishing one — these are those who were obedient and meek and gentle, not quarreling among themselves. They always rejoiced in the servants of God, and they clothed themselves in the Holy Spirit, and they always had mercy on every man, and gave of their own to everyone without reproach and without hesitation. **4** The Lord therefore sees their simplicity and their complete goodness, and filled them with the good things of his blessing, and they are worthy of eternal life because they were of good character and were innocent, and they toiled for the Lord's servants." **5** "Those from the eighth mountain — full of springs and having all manner of creatures of the Lord drinking from those springs — these are the apostles and teachers who preached to the whole world, teaching the word of the Lord in holiness and truth, and not giving way to any evil desires, but walking always in righteousness and truth. **6** These therefore are in peace with one another always. Therefore they are established in peace and will live to God." **7** "Those from the ninth mountain, which was a wilderness full of serpents and beasts that destroy men — these are the deacons who administered badly, who stole the substance of widows and orphans, and who made gain for themselves from the service which they had undertaken. If they abide in the same desire, they shall die and have no hope of life; but if they turn and complete their ministries with purity, they shall have the possibility of life." **8** "Those from the tenth mountain — the one entirely shaded with trees under which sheep were resting — these are the bishops and hospitable people who always received into their houses with joy the servants of God, without hypocrisy. These bishops at all times sheltered the afflicted and the widows in their service, and they behaved with holiness in all things. **9** All these therefore will be sheltered by the Lord for ever. Those who did these things are glorious before God, and their place is already with the angels, if they keep the commandments of the Lord." **10** "Those from the eleventh mountain — the fruit-bearing one — these are those who suffered for the name of the Lord and who gave up their lives and goods gladly and with their whole hearts, and suffered willingly for the name of the Lord." **11** "Those from the twelfth mountain — the entirely white one — these are the innocent ones, the babes in faith, into whose heart no evil came, nor did they know what wickedness was. They always remained in childlike innocence. **12** These therefore will rest for ever and without doubt live with God. Blessed are you all who put away wickedness from yourselves and put on innocence — you shall live to God first of all."

---

*EMET note: Vision 3.13 completes the twelve-mountain typology (mountains 6-12). The twelfth mountain (entirely white = innocent babes) is the ideal category, ending on an eschatological beatitude.*
